clue.text: Caddish leader in Nash's city set

indicators.note: the leader letter sits inside the city's name, so 'in' marks a container

parts.note: Beau Nash was the famous master of ceremonies at Bath, the Georgian spa city in Somerset

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so we take the opening letter of Caddish

explanation.surface: A cad's ringleader belongs to the fashionable set of Regency Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Beau Nash ran society in Bath, the English spa town; 'leader' gives C from Caddish, put 'in' BATH.
explanation.definitionFit: A batch is a group of things produced or dealt with together, a collection.

clue.text: Reverses promise to supply weapon

parts.note: to reverse a vehicle is to back it, so reverses gives backs
giving your word is making a promise

explanation.surface: Someone goes back on a pledge to provide arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A backsword is a sword with only one sharp edge, a single-edged blade.

clue.text: Italian city-can include an ancient one

indicators.note: the tin container is said to take in the old city, so include marks one piece inside another

parts.note: a can is a tin
one refers back to city: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city of crosswords

explanation.surface: An Italian town is said to be able to embrace an old settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' points back to 'city', so 'an ancient one' is UR, the Sumerian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is the Piedmontese capital in northern Italy, home of Fiat and the Shroud.

clue.text: Passes the fish by way of greeting ?

parts.note: to hand something is to pass it over
hake is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Someone hands over a fish as a way of saying hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking hands is a customary salutation on meeting.

clue.text: Marine craft?

parts.note: read as a seagoing vessel, but a Royal Marine is nicknamed a Jolly, so this is a vessel belonging to such a sailor

explanation.surface: A clue about a boat for the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' is old navy slang for a Royal Marine; the small ship's boat that carries the name fits both readings.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ship's boat used for ferrying crew is called by this name, so it is a vessel at sea.

clue.text: Pike spinner turns up in pool

parts.note: a jack is a young pike

indicators.note: in a down clue turning a word up reads it from the bottom, so the toy's name runs backwards

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy

explanation.surface: An angler's spinning lure lands a pike from the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: Pike, spinner and pool all suggest fishing; 'turns up' reverses TOP to POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool is an accumulated pot of stakes, the big prize in a game or lottery.

clue.text: Makes Lee star in Hamlet

indicators.note: the actor's name and star are worked into something new, so makes signals rearranging

explanation.surface: An actor called Lee is turned into a star by playing in Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes' tells you to remake the letters of LEE STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Laertes, son of Polonius and brother of Ophelia, is a character in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Swift horse's stableman ?

parts.note: Swift is Jonathan Swift: in Gulliver's Travels the rational horses keep brutish human creatures as servants, read as a fast horse's groom

explanation.surface: A question about who grooms a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like 'fast', but it is the author: in Gulliver's Travels the Houyhnhnms, a race of rational horses, rule over the brutish humans.
explanation.definitionFit: These brutish people serve the noble horses in Gulliver's fourth voyage, as their underlings.

clue.text: One gets (in UK) forty-eight ducks-huge number

definitions.text: One gets (in UK) forty-eight ducks-huge number

parts.words: One gets (in UK) forty-eight ducks-huge number
parts.note: duck is cricket's zero, so the figure one followed by forty-eight noughts is the British form of an enormous number

explanation.surface: A batsman is out for nought forty-eight times.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so one with 48 noughts after it is 10 to the power 48: the old British (long-scale) value.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British long scale this numeral is a million raised to the eighth power, a gigantic quantity.

clue.text: This building worker said to be a revolting type

indicators.note: the name is heard rather than seen, so said to be marks a word spoken aloud

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, a rebel

explanation.surface: A builder is rumoured to be a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt in 1381; 'revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who lays roof or floor tiles works on buildings.

clue.text: " To suckle fools and small beer " (Othello)

definitions.text: " To suckle fools and small beer " (Othello)

parts.words: To suckle fools and small beer
parts.note: Iago's line in Othello reads 'to suckle fools and ___ small beer': the clue omits the verb meaning record

explanation.surface: A quotation from Othello with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Iago's speech in Act 2 says a woman's worth is 'To suckle fools and chronicle small beer', i.e. to record trivia.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to record events in order, as a historian does.

clue.text: Vicki's grand establishment

parts.note: Vicki Baum wrote the novel filmed as Grand ___, so her grand establishment is a big place to stay

explanation.surface: A woman named Vicki owns an impressive business.
explanation.walkthrough: Vicki Baum's novel became the 1932 film Grand Hotel; 'grand' does double duty as title word and adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn or lodging house is an establishment offering rooms to guests.

clue.text: Cavity heater is returned

indicators.note: something returned comes back, so the whole phrase is read in reverse order

parts.note: the sun heats the earth

explanation.surface: A heater that was faulty has been taken back to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' reverses SUN IS as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is an air-filled hollow in the bones of the skull.

clue.text: Uninspired literary work-needs some fire ?

explanation.surface: A dull book would be better burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: something that boils a pot needs a fire beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack piece written just to earn money; and literally a vessel for heating water, which needs flames under it.

clue.text: Ham finished by wild-cat

parts.note: when something is over it is finished

indicators.note: a wild animal runs out of control, so the letters of cat are scattered

explanation.surface: A joint of ham is finished off by a feral cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ham' looks like meat but is a showy actor; 'wild' rearranges CAT to ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to perform in an exaggerated way, playing a part too broadly.

clue.text: Former quarter associated with Whistler, possibly

parts.note: E for east, one of the four quarters of the compass

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the name may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: An old district linked with the painter Whistler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter' suggests a district but gives E, a compass point; 'possibly' rearranges WHISTLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile is an old-fashioned word for previous or one-time.

clue.text: Vandals went in for this material

explanation.surface: The barbarian Vandals were keen on cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vandals sacked Rome in AD 455, so plundering was their business.
explanation.definitionFit: Plundering a city is what the barbarians did; and coarse cloth such as hessian is a fabric.

clue.text: Ruth's poetical standing-ground ?

parts.note: Keats's nightingale ode pictures the biblical Ruth standing in tears amid the alien corn, so her place in poetry is a field of grain

explanation.surface: Asking where a woman called Ruth stands in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Keats, Ode to a Nightingale: 'the sad heart of Ruth, when, sick for home, She stood in tears amid the alien corn.'
explanation.definitionFit: A field growing wheat or other grain is where the gleaner Ruth stood.

clue.text: Foreign article produced by plant

parts.note: German stands for a foreign language and nationality
der is the German masculine definite article, equivalent to 'the'

explanation.surface: An imported newspaper article was written by a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: The article is foreign too: DER is German for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Germander is a herb of the mint family, genus Teucrium.

clue.text: The course to leave, say ?

indicators.note: say indicates the word is spoken, so we want a sound-alike

parts.note: to desert is to abandon or leave

explanation.surface: Is this the route to depart on?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a route; here it is part of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet served at the end of dinner is one of its courses.

clue.text: National' emblem-possibly it's the pound

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be in a different order

parts.note: L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: Perhaps a nation's symbol is its currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges ITSTHE with L (pound).
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly plant is Scotland's national symbol.

clue.text: Associate makes some point about retiring

parts.note: part means some of something
N, north, a compass point

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the two letters for about are reversed

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A colleague makes a remark about stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' reverses RE (about) to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is a colleague, someone associated in a business or venture.

clue.text: Show attendant a collection of books

parts.note: a page is a boy attendant
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A library assistant displays a set of volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: NT is the New Testament, itself a collection of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a spectacular public procession or display.

clue.text: What a fiddler will do, or an archer will use

explanation.surface: Fiddlers and archers have something in common.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first as two words: a violinist will bow (each) string.
explanation.definitionFit: A violinist draws the bow across each wire; and an archer draws back the cord of the bow.

clue.text: Creature from a Birkenhead quarter

parts.note: read as Birken head, the first letter of Birken, B
east is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: An animal from a district of Birkenhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Birkenhead is a town on Merseyside; split it as 'Birken-head' for its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A beast is an animal.

clue.text: Pollution ? Commonly it is not

explanation.surface: Someone questions whether there is any pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks dialect speech: it ain't, contracted.
explanation.definitionFit: Contamination or a stain is a corruption; and a colloquial contraction of 'it ain't' says it isn't.

clue.text: Girl gives a refusal if taken aback

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the whole phrase a refusal if is read in reverse

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: A girl says no if she is startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' looks like surprise; it reverses A NO IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiona is a girl's name, popular in Scotland.

clue.text: One among numbers rejected by the Head

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
among says the one goes in the middle of the numbers

parts.note: No. is short for number; two of them give NONO
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man is turned down by the headmaster as one of many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' gives NO NO (two Nos.), I goes 'among' them, then 'rejected' reverses NOINO.
explanation.definitionFit: Onion is old slang for the head, as in 'off one's onion'.

clue.text: Excuse — I am neither Tory nor Labour

parts.note: a member of the third party, the Liberals, is a Lib, so a Lib

explanation.surface: A voter excuses themself from both main parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I am a Lib' backwards in order: A LIB, then I; the Liberals were Britain's third party.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea that you were elsewhere is offered as an excuse.

clue.text: It helped sailing craft to turn

parts.note: a craft or trade is a skilled occupation
to wind is to turn, as a key or handle

explanation.surface: A sailing boat is being turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat but means a trade; 'sailing craft' is not one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady prevailing breeze in the tropics carried merchant sailing ships.

clue.text: Handling that removes ill-feeling?

explanation.surface: Careful handling dispels resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-feeling' suggests resentment; read literally it is feeling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing with something is handling it; and medical care cures sickness.

clue.text: Foreign currency, in the ordinary way down

indicators.note: the money sits inside the word ordinary, so in marks letters concealed there

explanation.surface: Money from abroad goes down in the usual way.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits within 'ordinary'.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is the monetary unit of several countries, such as Kuwait and Serbia.
